verses.text: How lonely the city sits, the city once so full of people! She who was great among the nations has become like a widow. She who was a princess among the provinces has become a slave.
She weeps bitterly at night, with tears on her cheeks. Among all her lovers there is no one to comfort her. All her friends have betrayed her. They have become her enemies.
Judah has gone into exile after suffering and hard slavery. She lives among the nations but finds no rest. All who chased her caught her in her distress.
The roads to Zion mourn, because no one comes to the festivals. All her gates are deserted. Her priests groan. Her young women grieve, and she herself is in bitter pain.
Her enemies have become her masters. Her enemies are doing well, because the LORD has made her suffer for her many sins. Her children have been taken captive by the enemy.
All the splendor has left the daughter of Zion. Her leaders have become like deer that find no pasture. They have run away without strength in front of the hunter.

In the days of her suffering and wandering, Jerusalem remembers all the treasures she had in days gone by. When her people fell into enemy hands, no one helped her. Her enemies looked at her and laughed at her ruin.
Jerusalem has sinned terribly, so she has become unclean. All who once honored her now look down on her, because they have seen her naked. She herself groans and turns away.
Her filth clung to her skirts. She did not think about her future. Her fall was shocking, and no one is there to comfort her. "LORD, look at my suffering, for the enemy has won!"
The enemy has laid his hands on all her treasures. She watched as the nations entered her holy place, the very people you commanded not to enter your assembly.
All her people groan as they search for bread. They trade their treasures for food to stay alive. "LORD, look and see how I am despised."
"Does this mean nothing to you, all you who pass by? Look and see if there is any pain like the pain brought on me, which the LORD made me suffer on the day of his fierce anger.
From on high he sent fire into my bones, and it overpowered them. He spread a net for my feet and turned me back. He has left me ruined and faint all day long.
My sins have been tied into a yoke by his hand. They are woven together and put on my neck. He has taken away my strength. The Lord has handed me over to those I cannot fight.
The Lord has rejected all the warriors among me. He has called an army against me to crush my young men. The Lord has trampled young Judah as grapes are trampled in a winepress.
This is why I weep. My eyes overflow with tears, because the one who could comfort me and give me strength is far away. My children are ruined, because the enemy has won."
Zion reaches out her hands, but there is no one to comfort her. The LORD has ordered that Jacob's neighbors become his enemies. Jerusalem has become something unclean among them.
"The LORD is right, because I rebelled against his command. Listen, all you peoples, and look at my pain. My young women and young men have gone into exile.
I called to my lovers, but they betrayed me. My priests and elders died in the city while searching for food to stay alive.
LORD, look how distressed I am! My stomach is in knots. My heart is broken inside me, because I have been so rebellious. Out in the street the sword kills. Inside the house there is only death.

People have heard my groaning, but there is no one to comfort me. All my enemies have heard about my trouble, and they are glad that you have done this. Bring the day you have announced, so that they will become like me.
Let all their wickedness come before you. Deal with them as you have dealt with me because of all my sins. For my groans are many, and my heart is weak."
